name: Abraham Lincoln Lies 10 Feet Underground in a Reinforced Concrete Vault
subtitle: Lincoln Tomb State Historic Site, Oak Ridge Cemetery, Springfield, IL. Bronze nose on bust rubbed gold by millions of visitors
description: Lincoln died on 15 April 1865, shot the previous evening at Ford's Theatre by John Wilkes Booth, just five days after Confederate General Lee surrendered at Appomattox. Lincoln's body was reinterred multiple times before being permanently sealed in 1901 beneath 10 feet of concrete inside the Oak Ridge Cemetery monument. In 1876, thieves nearly stole the coffin to hold it for ransom, prompting the reinforced burial. Mary Todd Lincoln and three of their four sons are entombed alongside him.
address: Oak Ridge Cemetery, 1441 Monument Ave, Springfield, IL 62702, United States

name: Alexander Hamilton Is Buried Steps from Wall Street, Killed by His Vice President
subtitle: Trinity Churchyard, 74 Trinity Pl, New York, NY. White marble tomb beneath a towering oak
description: On 12 July 1804, Alexander Hamilton died from a pistol wound inflicted the previous morning by sitting Vice President Aaron Burr during a duel in Weehawken, New Jersey. Hamilton was buried at Trinity Churchyard in Lower Manhattan, mere blocks from the financial district he designed. The white marble tomb bears a lengthy epitaph praising his patriotism and genius. Burr, who ordered the duel after Hamilton publicly opposed his gubernatorial campaign, was never tried for murder and outlived Hamilton by 32 years.
address: Trinity Churchyard, 74 Trinity Place, New York, NY 10006, United States

name: Billy the Kid Is Buried Behind Iron Bars at Old Fort Sumner Cemetery
subtitle: Old Fort Sumner Cemetery, Fort Sumner, NM. Grave shared with two outlaws, caged in iron to stop theft
description: Billy the Kid was shot dead by Sheriff Pat Garrett on 14 July 1881 in Fort Sumner, New Mexico, at just 21 years old. He is buried at Old Fort Sumner Cemetery alongside fellow outlaws Tom O'Folliard and Charlie Bowdre, the shared headstone reading 'Pals.' The grave is enclosed in a heavy iron cage, installed after the original marker was stolen three times. The outlaw who escaped two jails in life has spent over a century locked inside one in death.
address: Old Fort Sumner Cemetery, Billy the Kid Road, Fort Sumner, NM 88119, United States

name: Charles Dickens Buried in Poet's Corner Against His Own Wishes for a Simple Grave
subtitle: Westminster Abbey, 20 Deans Yd, Westminster, London. Plain stone slab inscribed with name alone
description: Dickens died on 09 June 1870 from a cerebral hemorrhage, collapsing at dinner after a full day of writing. Despite his explicit instructions for a modest funeral with no public announcement, Westminster Abbey claimed the burial. The grave slab in Poet's Corner bears only his name and dates, honoring his wish for simplicity. Crowds in New York reportedly wept in the streets when news arrived, mourning the man who had made the poor visible to the Victorian world.
address: Westminster Abbey, 20 Deans Yard, Westminster, London SW1P 3PA, United Kingdom

name: Edgar Allan Poe Is Buried Twice, His Second Grave Marked by a Raven
subtitle: Westminster Hall and Burying Ground, 519 W Fayette St, Baltimore, MD. White marble monument near the front gate
description: Poe died on 07 October 1849 in Baltimore, delirious and wearing clothes that were not his own, cause of death still unknown after 175 years. Originally buried in an unmarked back corner of Westminster Burying Ground, Poe was exhumed and reinterred in 1875 beneath a large marble monument near the entrance. The original grave still exists and still draws visitors. Every year from 1949 to 2009, an anonymous figure in black left three roses and a bottle of cognac at the grave on Poe's birthday.
address: 519 W Fayette St, Baltimore, MD 21201, United States

name: Karl Marx Lies Beneath a Bronze Bust Funded by Communist Parties Worldwide
subtitle: Highgate Cemetery East, Swain's Lane, London N6 6PJ. Towering bronze bust atop a granite plinth inscribed 'Workers of All Lands Unite'
description: Marx died on 14 March 1883 in London, found dead in his armchair weeks after the death of his eldest daughter, having never recovered from grief and illness. He was buried in Highgate Cemetery with only eleven mourners present. In 1954 the Communist Party of Great Britain exhumed his remains and reinterred them under a massive monument erected in 1956, paid for by communist parties internationally. The man who died penniless now rests beneath a monument that charges visitors an entry fee to approach.
address: Highgate Cemetery East, Swain's Lane, London N6 6PJ, United Kingdom

name: Marie Curie Dies from the Radiation That Made Her Famous
subtitle: Panthéon, Paris, France. Crypt shared with Pierre; coffin lined with inch-thick lead shielding
description: Marie Curie died on 04 July 1934 from aplastic anemia caused by decades of radiation exposure, often carrying test tubes of radioactive isotopes in her coat pockets. Curie was interred alongside her husband Pierre in the Panthéon crypt in 1995, becoming the first woman entombed there on her own merit. Her personal notebooks from the 1890s remain so radioactive that researchers must sign a liability waiver and wear protective gear to read them.
address: Panthéon, Place du Panthéon, 75005 Paris, France

name: Muhammad Ali Buried in Louisville Soil He Once Threatened to Throw His Gold Medal Into
subtitle: Cave Hill Cemetery, 701 Baxter Ave, Louisville, KY. Flat granite marker engraved simply: Muhammad Ali
description: Muhammad Ali died on 03 June 2016 in Scottsdale, Arizona, after a 32-year battle with Parkinson's disease that had reduced the most voluble athlete in history to near silence. Ali was buried at Cave Hill Cemetery in Louisville, the city where Cassius Clay was born and where, as an 18-year-old Olympic gold medalist, he reportedly threw his medal into the Ohio River after being refused service at a whites-only restaurant. The grave marker is deliberately plain, bearing only his name. A public funeral procession carried the casket through Louisville streets lined with tens of thousands.
address: Cave Hill Cemetery, 701 Baxter Avenue, Louisville, KY 40204, United States

name: Theodore Roosevelt Buried Simply at Youngs Memorial Cemetery, No State Funeral
subtitle: Youngs Memorial Cemetery, Oyster Bay, NY. Plain headstone on a wooded hillside near his Sagamore Hill estate
description: Roosevelt died in his sleep on 06 January 1919 at Sagamore Hill, aged 60, from a pulmonary embolism after years of deteriorating health following jungle expeditions and war injuries. Buried at Youngs Memorial Cemetery just miles from his beloved estate, the grave is marked by a modest rough-cut granite stone, a deliberate contrast to the grand monuments of other presidents. Roosevelt had explicitly refused a state funeral, insisting on a small private burial. Vice President Thomas Marshall remarked upon hearing the news: 'Death had to take him sleeping, for if Roosevelt had been awake there would have been a fight.'
address: Youngs Memorial Cemetery, 14 Cove Road, Oyster Bay, NY 11771, United States

name: David Livingstone's Heart Is Buried in Africa, His Body in Westminster Abbey
subtitle: Westminster Abbey, 20 Broad Sanctuary, Westminster, London. Black marble slab set into the nave floor
description: Livingstone died on 01 May 1873, found kneeling in prayer beside his bed in Chitambo village, present-day Zambia. His attendants removed his heart and buried it under a mpundu tree before carrying his embalmed body 1,500 miles to the coast. The body was shipped to London and interred beneath a black marble slab in the nave of Westminster Abbey, inscribed with his own words against the slave trade. The cotton-mill boy who walked 29,000 miles across Africa now rests among kings.
address: Westminster Abbey, 20 Broad Sanctuary, Westminster, London SW1P 3PA, United Kingdom

name: Rosa Parks Rests in Detroit, Far from the Montgomery Bus She Never Left
subtitle: Woodlawn Cemetery, 19975 Woodward Ave, Detroit, MI. Crypt in the Chapel of Remembrance mausoleum
description: Rosa Parks died on 24 October 2005 in her Detroit apartment at age 92, having lived with progressive dementia in her final years. Parks is interred in the Chapel of Remembrance mausoleum at Woodlawn Cemetery alongside her husband Raymond and her brother Sylvester McCauley. The mausoleum crypt bears her full name, Rosa Louise McCauley Parks. In a striking reversal, the woman arrested for refusing to move was honored with a lying-in-state at the U.S. Capitol Rotunda, only the 31st person in American history to receive that distinction.
address: 19975 Woodward Ave, Detroit, MI 48203, United States

name: Thomas Edison Buried Near the Lab Where He Reinvented the World
subtitle: Rosedale Cemetery, 408 Main St, Orange, NJ. Simple granite marker beside his second wife, Mina.
description: Thomas Edison died on 18 October 1931 at age 84 from complications of diabetes at his Glenmont estate in West Orange, New Jersey. He is buried at Rosedale Cemetery beside his second wife, Mina Miller Edison, beneath a modest granite stone that lists no patents and no inventions. President Herbert Hoover asked Americans to dim their electric lights for one minute in tribute, a gesture made possible entirely by Edison's own technology.
address: Rosedale Cemetery, 408 Main St, Orange, NJ 07050, United States

name: Daniel Burnham Rests in the City He Reimagined, Beside a Glacial Boulder
subtitle: Graceland Cemetery, 4001 N Clark St, Chicago, IL. Grave marked by a massive glacial erratic on a wooded island
description: Daniel Burnham died on 01 June 1912 in Heidelberg, Germany, from complications of food poisoning, while traveling abroad. He is buried on a small wooded island within Graceland Cemetery, his grave marked by an uncut glacial boulder — a deliberately rough counterpoint to the polished neoclassical grandeur he imposed on Chicago's lakefront in 1893. The White City he conjured from swampland lasted only one summer before burning, yet reshaped American urban ambition permanently.
address: Graceland Cemetery, 4001 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60613, United States

name: Carl Friedrich Gauss Lies Beneath a 17-Sided Polygon Carved in Stone
subtitle: Albanifriedhof, Göttingen, Niedersachsen, Germany. Headstone engraved with a heptadecagon, his proudest discovery
description: Gauss died on 23 February 1855 in Göttingen, aged 77, of heart failure. He is buried at Albanifriedhof beneath a monument bearing the 17-sided regular polygon he proved constructible at age 19, a feat he considered his greatest achievement. The stonemason reportedly found the heptadecagon so difficult to distinguish from a circle that he carved a 17-pointed star instead. Gauss had kept dozens of major theorems unpublished during his lifetime, deeming them unready, and later mathematicians spent decades rediscovering results already sitting in his private notebooks.
address: Albanifriedhof, Kasseler Landstraße, 37081 Göttingen, Niedersachsen, Germany

name: FDR Is Buried in His Rose Garden, Never Revealing He Used a Wheelchair
subtitle: Home of Franklin D. Roosevelt NHS, 4097 Albany Post Rd, Hyde Park, NY. White marble slab in family rose garden
description: Franklin Roosevelt died of a cerebral hemorrhage on 12 April 1945 in Warm Springs, Georgia, just weeks before Germany's surrender. He is buried beneath a plain white marble slab in the rose garden at Springwood, his Hyde Park estate, alongside Eleanor. The grave bears only their names and birth and death years. Roosevelt concealed the full extent of his paralysis from the public throughout his presidency, yet the nation that never saw him walk mourned him as the man who carried them through depression and world war.
address: 4097 Albany Post Road, Hyde Park, New York 12538, United States

name: Dick Hickock Hanged for a Safe That Never Existed at Mount Muncie Cemetery
subtitle: Mount Muncie Cemetery, Leavenworth, KS. Buried in the same county where he was executed at Lansing State Penitentiary
description: Dick Hickock was hanged at Lansing State Penitentiary on 14 April 1965, alongside Perry Smith, for the 1959 murders of the Clutter family in Holcomb, Kansas. The robbery that triggered the killings was planned around a prison cellmate's tip about a safe full of cash. No safe existed. Hickock, once a standout high school football player, was buried at Mount Muncie Cemetery in Leavenworth. In 2012, researchers exhumed both Hickock and Smith to collect DNA in connection with an unsolved Florida family murder, a case that ultimately went cold.
address: Mount Muncie Cemetery, 100 Muncie Road, Leavenworth, KS 66048, United States

name: Winston Churchill Buried in a Village Churchyard, Not Westminster Abbey
subtitle: St Martin's Church, Bladon, Oxfordshire. Simple family plot beside his parents, Lord and Lady Randolph Churchill
description: Churchill died on 24 January 1965, aged 90, exactly 70 years after his father. Despite lying in state at Westminster Hall for three days, drawing 321,000 mourners, Churchill was buried not among kings at Westminster Abbey but in the quiet churchyard at Bladon, Oxfordshire, yards from Blenheim Palace where he was born. The plain Portland stone slab reads only his name and dates. The man who saved an empire rests in a country parish.
address: St Martin's Church, Church Road, Bladon, Woodstock, Oxfordshire OX20 1RS, United Kingdom
